statements.statement: Each short row on a breadboard typically has 5 holes connected internally.
statements.explanation: Underneath the breadboard, metal strips connect each short row of 5 holes together, so inserting components into the same row links them electrically.

statements.statement: Rows on the left side of the center gap connect to rows on the right side.
statements.explanation: The center gap splits the board in two: rows on the left don't connect to rows on the right. This gap is sized to fit chips that straddle both sides.

statements.statement: You need to solder components onto a breadboard to make connections.
statements.explanation: Breadboards are designed for solderless prototyping. You build circuits by pushing wires and components into holes, with no soldering needed.
